the following aspects.

the following: (a) the use of the QUASAR ASL sequence for the estimation of cerebral blood flow (CBF) and the arterial arrival time (AAT) in the human brain using a stable spline approach (SSA); (b) a comparison of the SSA with the oSVD‐ED approach using simulated data; and (c) the application of both methods to real data and the evaluation of the results using a visual inspection.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we introduce a novel deconvolution method for QUASAR ASL that is based on the combination of stable spline and oSVD.
we developed a novel method for the estimation of arterial arrival time (AT), impulse response function (IRF) and perfusion (CBF) from QUASAR‐ASL data.
we introduce a new method to estimate the arterial arrival time and the impulse response function using QUASAR ASL data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of stable spline for the regularization of the impulse response function can improve perfusion estimation and the estimation of the arterial arrival time.

the proposed method is a promising alternative to the oSVD‐ED approach, with a better performance in terms of the bias in perfusion estimation and a comparable performance in terms of standard deviation.
